title: Best Beard Trimmers UK
short: Eight beard trimmers tested on real facial hair over several days, from a £27 budget workhorse to a £130 waterproof premium model.
intro: A beard trimmer needs to cut evenly without snagging, navigate the contours of a face, and last through a full trim without running flat. This guide is based on Expert Reviews' tested roundup (updated December 2025), where each trimmer was tried on thick, bushy facial hair around 2cm long, then again several days later on new growth, judging cutting lengths, precision, charge time, battery performance, ergonomics and value. Prices are as reviewed.

products.name: Barba
products.best_for: Anyone who wants a simple, reliable trimmer that lasts for years
products.key_spec: 1.5-18mm cutting range, 9 length increments, ceramic blades, 40-minute usage time, mains-usable when flat
products.summary: Expert Reviews' Best Buy: a mechanical adjustment wheel makes choosing from nine trimming lengths easy, with only one clip-on comb so there's nothing to lose, and ceramic blades that never need oiling. It cuts evenly every time without snagging. The reviewer's own decade-old example still works; his main gripe is battery life, though it can be used plugged into the mains, and a lithium-ion version lasting up to an hour costs £38.
pros: Excellent value under £30
No snagging, cuts evenly every time
Ceramic blades need no oiling
cons: Battery could last longer between charges

products.name: Aqua Blade
products.best_for: The closest possible trim, including in the shower
products.key_spec: 0.2-25mm cutting range, 12 guide combs, waterproof, 3-hour usage time, 1-hour charge
products.summary: Wahl claims this is the only beard trimmer you'll ever need, and Expert Reviews found the closeness of its cut backs that up: it's the nearest you'll get to shaving without a foil or wet shaver. After several months of use the reviewer was most impressed by cut closeness, and it's showerproof with a 3-hour battery life. There's no guard, so the reviewer cut himself a couple of times when he didn't pull his neck skin taut.
pros: Cuts twice as close as rivals, to 0.2mm
Waterproof for use in the shower
Lasts an impressive 3 hours between charges
cons: No guard, so there's a cut risk without careful use

products.name: BT5260
products.best_for: A brilliant all-round trimmer without spending a fortune
products.key_spec: 1-20mm cutting range, 39 length increments in 0.5mm steps, AutoSensing power, washable, free razor included
products.summary: Expert Reviews found excellent, effortless results thanks to Braun's AutoSensing technology, which adjusts power to the beard's thickness. It can be approached from any direction without precise positioning and cuts smoothly and evenly with zero snagging, plus a detail-trimmer attachment for neat lines and a free Gillette razor in the box, making it the best value on the list. Thinner hairs occasionally clogged the comb when used on head hair.
pros: Versatile with smooth, even cuts from any angle
AutoSensing technology adjusts to beard thickness
Comes with a detail trimmer and free razor
cons: Thinner hairs can clog the comb

products.name: Beard Trimmer 9000 Prestige
products.best_for: A weighty, premium-feeling trimmer for shorter, well-groomed styles
products.key_spec: 0.2-10mm cutting range, 30 length increments, steel comb, fully waterproof, 2-hour usage time
products.summary: Expert Reviews found a steel comb that doesn't flex under pressure like plastic rivals, with a chunky metallic design that feels reassuringly weighty. It's fully waterproof for use and cleaning in the shower, and battery performance is solid at two hours from an hour's charge. With a maximum length of 10mm, it isn't the best choice for longer beards.
pros: Great construction, doesn't flex like plastic rivals
Fully waterproof
Solid 2-hour battery life
cons: Not the best choice for longer beards

products.name: ER-CKN1 MULTISHAPE Modular Personal Care System
products.best_for: Anyone who wants one main unit that expands to cover every grooming task
products.key_spec: 1-20mm cutting range, 39 length increments, modular attachment system (nose trimmer, shaver, toothbrush), waterproof
products.summary: Expert Reviews found one of the most innovative and best-looking trimmers tested: buy the main unit, then add attachments for nose trimming, shaving or even an electric toothbrush. It powered through beard hair without any problem and was an absolute dream to hold, with a sleek matt finish that feels built to last. It isn't the cheapest option tested.
pros: Highly customisable with attachments for every grooming task
Powers through beard hair with no problems
Sleek design, feels built to last
cons: Not the cheapest option if you just want a basic trimmer

products.name: OneBlade 360 For Face
products.best_for: Precision edging and packing small for trips
products.key_spec: 0.5-9mm cutting range, 12 length settings, 360 flexing blade, fully waterproof, USB charging
products.summary: Expert Reviews found this compact hybrid trimmer/shaver, not much bigger than a fat cigar, the best tool they've tried for defining beard lines around the neck, chin and cheeks. The 360 Blade flexes in all directions to keep constant skin contact, and it's designed so it's almost impossible to nick yourself. The blade needs replacing roughly every four months, at around £25 for a pack of three.
pros: Great for travel due to its small size
Excellent for precision edging around the neck and cheeks
Variety of settings, fully waterproof
cons: Blade needs replacing roughly every 4 months, an ongoing cost

products.name: SuperStubble XTP Beard Trimmer
products.best_for: Precision-focused users who want a digital display and a flexible head
products.key_spec: 0.4-5mm cutting range in 0.2mm increments, digital display, floating flexible head, fully waterproof
products.summary: Expert Reviews found a great range of lengths adjustable in fine 0.2mm increments, with a digital display showing the exact length in use and remembering the last setting. The floating, flexible head follows facial contours a bit like an electric shaver head, making the trim feel a little more comfortable, though it didn't necessarily speed things up. Best suited to those who want hi-tech features rather than a basic, no-frills trimmer.
pros: Advanced digital features with precise 0.2mm adjustment
Flexible head follows facial contours
Battery life display shows remaining cutting time
cons: Not for those wanting a basic, no-frills trimmer

products.name: G4 Graphite Trimmer
products.best_for: One trimmer that covers beard, head, body, nose and eyebrows
products.key_spec: 1.5-20mm beard range, two fixed combs, nose/ear/eyebrow trimmer, mini foil and TST attachment, storage pouch
products.summary: Expert Reviews found a versatile trimmer that does it all: two fixed combs for face, head or body, an adjustable 2-20mm beard and hair comb, a nose, ear and eyebrow trimmer, a mini foil attachment and a close-trim TST attachment, all in a soft storage pouch. It trims beards from 1.5mm (or shorter without the comb) up to 20mm and did a decent job across the range tested. It has a slower charge time than others and isn't waterproof.
pros: Versatile selection of attachments for face, head, body and nose
Tailors to a wide range of grooming needs
Handy storage pouch included

guide.q: What cutting range do I need?
guide.a: For designer stubble, a shorter maximum range like the Philips OneBlade (up to 9mm) or BaByliss SuperStubble (up to 5mm) is enough. For longer beards, the Wahl Aqua Blade (up to 25mm) or Braun BT5260 and Remington G4 (up to 20mm) give far more room to grow before you need a new trimmer.

guide.q: Is a waterproof trimmer worth it?
guide.a: If you like to trim in the shower or want easy rinse-clean, look for 'fully waterproof' models like the Wahl Aqua Blade, Philips 9000 Prestige, Panasonic MULTISHAPE, Philips OneBlade and BaByliss SuperStubble. The budget Remington Barba and Remington G4 aren't waterproof.

guide.q: How much battery life do I actually need?
guide.a: Most trimmers here run for over an hour, plenty for a single trim. The Wahl Aqua Blade leads with 3 hours, useful for travel without a charger, while the budget Remington Barba's shorter 40-minute runtime can be topped up by using it plugged into the mains.

If you want one tool for your whole grooming routine, the Panasonic MULTISHAPE and Remington G4 both add nose, ear, body or shaving attachments. If you just want a dedicated beard trimmer, the Remington Barba or Wahl Aqua Blade keep things simple.
